hold_text: src/runtime/live_review_due.py runs in ict-web-api (the live-review due list); the manager merges (approval sought from the manager, who holds operator authority this week).
why: WHY: at the 16:00Z judgement_cadence slot, alpaca_portfolio SLV pkg-2616d7fbc5134e2e (trade 7774, slv_trend_1h) was skipped with 'skipped_nothing_new: new closed bar but price moved 0.00 ATR < 0.5 since the last review' (/api/diag/live_review_due 16:36Z skipped_slots). The package's path history held ONE priced bar (event_coverage: '1 history bar(s) with a price; need 2'), dated at or before the last review (LR-20261118T1800Z, last_close 40.63). package_novelty() took that bar as both 'at the last review' and 'now', so it measured 0.00 while the price was 41.29 (prescreen last_price), |41.29-40.63|/0.4086 = 1.62 ATR. That is a blind skip dressed as a measured one, the case the docstring forbids. WHAT: when the newest history bar is not after the last review, return NEW with 'move unreadable (no history bar after the last review): reviewing', the same as the other unreadable branches. Test: tests/test_live_review_due.py::test_trigger_first_stale_history_is_unmeasured_not_zero_move fails on main and passes here; the file has 58 passed and 1 env failure (test_route_requires_diag_token needs fastapi, absent in this sandbox; it fails on main too). Effect: packages whose telemetry/history is stale get a review at their cadence slot instead of a silent skip. That adds packets, it doesn't remove them, and it changes no order path. Gates this adds or changes: none.
